definitions.meaning: a Dalmatian is a breed of dog with a white coat covered in black spots
a sweet in the British sense of a pudding: a suet pudding studded with currants, the dried fruit looking like spots

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: literally a dog with spots, and the British name of a currant-studded steamed suet pudding.

clue.text: Open coal fires I let go out

indicators.note: out signals the remaining letters coming out in a new order
the letter I is let go, released from the fodder, so it is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lets a coal fire die down, as if confessing to letting it go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let go' takes I out of COALFIRES, leaving COALFRES; 'out' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in the open air, outdoors, as in an open-air meal eaten outside.

clue.text: Brief message about an unfounded report

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the message is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: a card is a short written message, like a postcard or greetings card
taken as written

explanation.surface: A short note concerning some baseless rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a false or baseless story spread as news, a hoax rumour.

clue.text: On first of October turn collar up in Scotland

indicators.note: first of picks just the opening letter of the word October
turn up, in a down clue, means the word for collar is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to collar someone is to nab or arrest them

explanation.surface: Advice to turn your collar up against the cold from the first of October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn ... up' reverses NAB to BAN in this down entry; 'On' is a link. The definition simply locates the answer: a west-coast town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a port and resort town on the west coast of Scotland, so a place found there.

definitions.meaning: further shielding or insurance, something laid over as well
a fielder in the off-side position between cover point and mid-off in cricket

explanation.definitionFit: Literally more shielding, and also a cricket fielding position (and its fielder) on the off side between cover and mid-off.

clue.text: Presentation of laws to be amended

indicators.note: laws being amended are changed, here their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A bill presenting laws that are due to be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' rearranges all the letters of LAWS TO BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestowal is the act of presenting or conferring something, such as an award.

definitions.meaning: boastful or meaningless chatter, all wind
literally the scorching atmosphere above the desert

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for empty boasting, and literally the heated atmosphere above a desert.

definitions.meaning: the prefix of the folklore werewolf, a man who turns into a wolf
a past-tense form of to be, suggesting something that existed once but is no more

explanation.definitionFit: The prefix of werewolves, and the past form of to be, implying things no longer exist.

parts.note: reads like a stand-in office holder, but means the street receptacle that holds letters briefly until collection

explanation.definitionFit: A British red pillar-shaped postbox keeps posted letters only until the collection, so it holds mail temporarily.

parts.note: reads like a thief's instructions, but describes running off secretly with a lover to marry

explanation.definitionFit: To run away secretly with a lover, usually to get married without consent.

indicators.note: contains signals that the tin holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: food is preserved in a tin

indicators.note: variety suggests a different form, so the letters of rare are rearranged

explanation.surface: A national park that protects an unusual species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' turns RARE into ERRA, which goes inside TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Country in the sense of land or ground, as in open country, is terrain.

parts.note: to desert or betray is to rat
a nation or people can be called a race

explanation.surface: A desert country hosting a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sand dunes but is the verb to rat on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the fierce competitive struggle of working life.

clue.text: Facilitated return by stamped addressed envelope to editor

indicators.note: return signals the abbreviation is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: SAE is the standard British abbreviation for a stamped addressed envelope

explanation.surface: An author made a submission easier by enclosing a stamped addressed envelope for the editor's reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses SAE to EAS. In Britain writers enclosed an SAE so the editor could post a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: To facilitate something is to ease it, make it easier.

clue.text: Offer support to hospital areas in reverse order

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
wards are the sections of a hospital

explanation.surface: Funding hospital departments by working through them last to first.
explanation.definitionFit: Going backwards means proceeding from the end towards the start, in reverse order.

clue.text: He hopes to avoid getting chicken in the basket

definitions.text: He hopes to avoid getting chicken in the basket

parts.words: He hopes to avoid getting chicken in the basket
parts.note: chicken in a basket is a pub meal, but here the basket hangs below a hot-air balloon and the flier hopes not to lose his nerve

explanation.definitionFit: A person who flies hot-air balloons travels in a basket and should not be chicken, that is cowardly.

parts.note: to settle a bill is to pay it
men are workers, as in a crew of men
read as over time: T is the abbreviation for time, with the workers placed over it

explanation.surface: A community agreeing to pay its workforce for extra hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overtime' splits as 'over time': in a down entry MEN sits over T, the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is a place where people have settled, a small community or village.

parts.note: flat out means at full effort, while flat also hints at level, so it reads as making a maximum level effort

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for trying as hard as one possibly can, a maximum effort.

parts.note: to end is to finish
owing money means being in debt

explanation.surface: Someone happy to end up in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' is not eager here but the verb of drawing up a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Willing in the sense of leaving property by will, which is endowing heirs with it.

clue.text: Eleven free, take in work to make a packet

indicators.note: take in signals the anagram receiving the other piece inside it
free suggests the letters are loosened and rearranged

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Eleven people get time off, take on a job, and earn a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' turns ELEVEN into ENVELE; 'take in' places OP inside it, ENVEL + OP + E.
explanation.definitionFit: An envelope is a paper wrapper, a packet in which letters are posted.

clue.text: Piano passage used to complete one's education

parts.note: a grand is a large piano
a tour is a journey or passage through places

explanation.surface: A piano piece used to round off a music student's studies.
explanation.walkthrough: Wealthy young Britons once rounded off their education with a long tour of the cultural cities of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical European tour taken by young aristocrats as the finishing stage of their education.

clue.text: How one may be cast as Captain Bligh?

definitions.text: How one may be cast as Captain Bligh?

parts.words: How one may be cast as Captain Bligh?
parts.note: cast sounds like an acting role, but Bligh was set loose in a small boat by mutineers on the Bounty

explanation.definitionFit: After the mutiny on the Bounty, Captain Bligh was set loose in an open boat, floating at the mercy of the sea.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
IV is the Roman numeral for 4
I is the Roman numeral for 1
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' looks like people but means numerals: 100, 4, 1 and 50.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished manners are courteous ones, so polite and civil.

indicators.note: into signals that the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: cuts are injuries
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.definitionFit: Clouts are heavy blows, hard hits with the hand.

clue.text: Sort of victory for some who'd ran in difficulty

indicators.note: in difficulty suggests trouble, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A runner who struggled achieved only a narrow win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in difficulty' rearranges the letters of WHO'D RAN; 'for some' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A victory gained only with great effort and struggle is described this way.

parts.note: split the first word after its opening letter: the garden implements are what remain of footwear when the S is taken off

explanation.definitionFit: Garden tools for weeding; add an S at the front and you have shoes, hence the joke.

clue.text: Rough cowl on chimney in Scotland

parts.note: a cowl is a hood
lum is the Scots word for chimney

explanation.surface: A cowl fitted on top of a Scottish chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' is a noun here, a rough or thug; a cowl is also a chimney cap, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a violent ruffian, which is what a hoodlum is.

clue.text: Fit of petulance encountered in playing draughts?

definitions.meaning: in draughts (US checkers) a piece is forfeited this way when a player fails to make a capture

explanation.definitionFit: A sulky mood, and the draughts term for removing an opponent's piece that missed a compulsory capture.

indicators.note: in places the student inside the reshaped word
form suggests shaping, so the letters of fine are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, so a student

explanation.surface: A naughty pupil who is in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' turns FINE into EFIN; 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means elf-like, and elves are playful and impish, so mischievous.

clue.text: The point of this device is not always apparent

definitions.text: The point of this device is not always apparent

parts.words: The point of this device is not always apparent
parts.note: reads like doubt over a gadget's purpose, but the sharp point is tucked away in a guard

explanation.definitionFit: A fastening pin whose sharp point clips into a cover so it stays hidden and cannot prick.
